name: Smart Calendar Hub
description:
Turns the clock menu into a side panel: tray icons, weather, date with a sky showing the real position of the sun and the moon, a calendar sized to the panel with your accounts' colours and the day's agenda, notifications, world clocks, alarms and timers. A click on a tray icon shows its menu inside the panel instead of a floating menu. A bell to silence an app, the IP addresses in the top bar, the battery as a ring, the accent colour on the top bar icons.

Clipboard: a click on an IP address in the panel, or on the copy button of a command in the settings, copies it to the clipboard; nothing is read from the clipboard.

Network use: only if you switch on "Public address" (off by default), the extension asks https://api.ipify.org for your public IP when the network changes and every 30 minutes. When you open "System updates", the update lists are read from your package mirrors and Flatpak remotes (checkupdates, flatpak), as the update programs do. Unless you switch off "Check for new versions", when you open the list of the settings, at most once a day, it asks api.github.com for the latest release of this extension; "Update" downloads that release from GitHub and installs it with gnome-extensions. Weather for the extra GNOME Weather cities you scroll to in the panel is downloaded the same way GNOME does it (MET Norway, METAR). Nothing else is sent anywhere.

Tray icons need the "AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support" extension. Events come from GNOME's online accounts (evolution-data-server); GNOME Calendar is used, if installed, to open events and create new ones.

Lock screen: only the look of the top bar (accent colour, space between the icons, clock position, battery) is kept; the side panel and everything personal are taken down while the screen is locked.

Other extensions can show their pages in the panel: see the README.

Designed and maintained by Michele, with code co-authored by Claude (Anthropic) under his direction; every change is tested by hand and reviewed.
